newsitem.title: GERMANY: German firms to create 300,000 jobs abroad-DIHT.
newsitem.headline: German firms to create 300,000 jobs abroad-DIHT.

text.p: German companies are planning foreign investments that should create at least 300,000 jobs in other countries by the end of 1999, the Federation of Chambers of Commerce (DIHT) said on Monday.
The plans to build new plants overseas will not necessarily result in cuts in German jobs, said DIHT, which drew its conclusions from a poll of business leaders.
New foreign plants would secure jobs in German factories producing pre-production materials and intermediate goods, DIHT said.

"The number of jobs at German firms in foreign countries will rise by at least 300,000 between the years 1997 and 1999," DIHT said. "This development is not inevitably connected to job losses at home."
DIHT said 28 percent of all western German companies plan to build plants overseas in the next three years.

Of those, 62 percent cited high domestic labour costs as their main motivation. High corporate taxes and business costs in Germany ranked as the second most important reasons for those adding locations abroad.
The DIHT estimate comes as Germany struggles with record unemployment and bickering by business, union and government heads over how to solve the problem.
German unemployment last month rose to a record 4.16 million, and was expected to reach about 4.5 million later this year.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl has set a goal of halving unemployment by 2000, but an "Alliance for Jobs" has so far failed to pull business and union leaders together.

Companies are mostly turning to Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic to lower production costs. Great Britain, the Netherlands and Austria also offer attractive combinations of labour costs and streamlined regulatory systems, DIHT said. Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax+44-171-542-5017
